newsitem.title: DUBAI: Crescent confirms stake sale to Taiwan monopoly.
newsitem.headline: Crescent confirms stake sale to Taiwan monopoly.

text.p: The United Arab Emirates' private Crescent Petroleum Co International Ltd on Tuesday confirmed that it had sold a minority stake for $75 million to Taiwan state oil monopoly Chinese Petroleum Corp.

Crescent said in a statement that it and Chinese Petroleum on Tuesday "established a strategic alliance and signed Share Purchase and Shareholder Agreements in which CPC will invest around $75 million in acquiring a minority stake in Crescent."

Chinese Petroleum announced the deal earlier on Tuesday in Taipei. The pact gives Chinese Petroleum access to 54 million barrels of oil reserves controlled by Crescent and to 14,000 barrels a day of Crescent's maximum daily production of 60,000.
In Taipei, Chinese Petroleum declined to to give a figure for how much control of Crescent the Taiwan monopoly would have.
Taiwan industry sources said Chinese Petroleum would have 40 percent of the private oil firm based in the emirate of Sharjah.
